text:
rahel: quick thread — experimenting with a 'nav handoff' for console deep links. idea: keep the primary path stable but let query+fragment pick out micro-views (tabs/anchors) without fully expanding the whole leftnav. want feedback on URL shape + accessibility.
owen: what URL shape are you thinking? path vs query vs hash?
rahel: canonical proposal: stable path + `?view=` for panel + optional `#fragment` for intra-panel anchors. e.g. `/console/workspaces/beta-9?view=usage#cpu` -> show workspace, open usage panel, jump to cpu. keeps breadcrumbs consistent.
yuki: accessibility: when we auto-open the view, we must set focus to the view heading and use `role=region aria-labelledby` so screen readers get context. also ensure `aria-live` for an announcement like "Usage panel opened" so users know something changed.
priya: agree. also for keyboard flow, save the origin element (data-return-id) before moving focus, so ESC or close returns focus predictably.
owen: history behaviour? please don't pollute the back stack when rewiring query params for tiny toggles. use `history.replaceState` for programmatic reveals and `pushState` for explicit navigations.
rahel: noted. example snippet I like: ```js
const u = new URL(location.href);
u.searchParams.set('view','usage');
history.replaceState({}, '', u);
```
yuki: breadcrumbs: if view opens we should append a breadcrumb crumb for it: `Console / Workspaces / beta-9 / Usage` — clickable to collapse. important for discoverability.
priya: shareability: if someone shares `/console/workspaces/beta-9?view=usage#cpu&highlight=cpu` the recipient should see a gentle pulse on the cpu row and an `aria-describedby` that says "Highlighted by link". respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
owen: perf: large dashboards may have many widgets. if `view=` present, prioritize hydrating that view component first, leave others lazy. show skeleton + `aria-busy=true` until content ready.
rahel: edge-case: resource not loaded (stale id) -> we should queue the view open until data resolves. i suggest a small deferred queue keyed by route so the action runs after fetch.
yuki: also ensure we don't scroll until the target element exists. `scrollIntoView({behavior: 'auto'})` + `element.focus({preventScroll:true})` then `element.scrollIntoView()` can help to manage focus+scroll timing.
priya: QA checklist for accessibility: keyboard-only path, SR announcement, focus-visible after programmatic focus, ESC return focus, skip-links still target main content when appropriate.
own-checker: route-scan detected similar patterns across `/console/*/:id` modules. recommend a shared client util `applyDeepView(params)` to centralize parsing, focus lifecycle, and analytics firing.
owen: analytics: emit `nav.handoff_open` with props {resource_path, view, fragment, via_deeplink:true, expanded_from_state:true/false}. helps measure whether deep views increase discovery.
rahel: UX question: should we auto-expand compressed groups in the leftnav when a deep link targets a child? or instead show a small inline indicator plus a toast "Open in leftnav"?
yuki: for accessibility and discoverability, auto-expand is better, but expansions should be session-only (not written to user's global prefs). also ensure DOM order exposes the focused item before moving focus.
priya: couple implementation nits: 1) normalize URLs (strip trailing slash, lowercase ids) to avoid duplicate share links; 2) when setting query param via replaceState, include `?view=` only when needed to keep URLs clean.
own-checker: suggested feature flag `console.nav_handoff` so we can toggle during experiments. also flagged potential collision with `console.sidecar` handlers; central util will help avoid double-handling.
owen: test matrix: unit tests for URL parsing, e2e for keyboard + SR flow, perf test for TTFI with view hydration.
rahel: i'll draft the pattern doc with canonical examples, code snippets for history API + focus helpers, a deferred action queue sketch, analytics schema, and the a11y QA checklist. will open PR and tag folks. can you review later today?
yuki: i'll take the a11y review.
priya: i'll review focus-return and keyboard flows.
own-checker: queued note: schedule route-scan after PR merge to validate no new overlaps.
rahel: thanks all — will post PR link here once ready :sparkles:
